idiom_name: private constructor + static create returning a Result union (or throwing)
implementation_notes: TypeScript's private modifier is compile-time only, but it is enough to keep the constructor out of application code, so the idiomatic factory is a static create method with a domain name that validates and returns either a Result union or a fully valid instance (throwing when the codebase uses exceptions), while branded ids stop raw strings from standing in for validated values. What replaces the classic factory class is the static method, or a module-level factory function; the functional variant returns a Result from a parse function instead of exposing a class at all.
pitfalls: private is erased at runtime: (order as any).constructor() and plain object literals can fake the shape, so validate at the boundary and treat the type as documentation.
Returning a Result while other code throws produces two error styles in one codebase; pick one per module and keep every factory consistent with it.
Class identity breaks across bundles and realms, so factory branching on instanceof should switch to a discriminant property.

variants.name: Smart-constructor parse function over branded ids (functional)
variants.implementation_notes: The functional realization drops the class: parse functions validate unknown input at the boundary, brand the result (a readonly __brand tag) and return a discriminated Result union, so the rest of the code only ever sees a value that has already passed the rules. Choose it when the codebase prefers data plus functions over classes, or when the input arrives as JSON from outside the process; the OO variant stays the better fit when the aggregate has rich behaviour and framework integration.
pitfalls: A brand is only as strong as its constructor: exporting the brand tag or an unchecked cast lets callers forge values and makes the parse step optional.
unknown is not validated by types; parse every field (zod/valibot/io-ts or hand-written guards) or the branded type is a lie.
